page: The Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is an entry-tier virtual server within the High Performance lineup, based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a nominal clock frequency of 2.0 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The cache structure consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. Memory capacity is fixed at 12.0 GB, allocating 3.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 260 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one public IPv4 address, with no dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-threaded execution. The platform achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1165.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1466.08, both registering in the average tier. Conversely, multi-threaded output placed in lower percentiles, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 3734.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6551.68. Memory bandwidth measured 421.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, tapering to 36.96 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 28.11 GB/sec for writes. The machine sustained 6.4 million Redis SET operations per second and reached 4.84 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The allocation of shared CPU threads introduces resource contention risks under persistent, parallel computational loads, which is reflected in reduced multi-threaded decompression and physics simulation metrics. Nonetheless, the inclusion of local NVMe storage and balanced memory density provides cost efficiency for lower-intensity workloads. Appropriate applications include moderate-traffic web servers, development environments, staging systems, and lightweight caching layers that do not saturate all vCPUs simultaneously.
description: The Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a virtual instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.0 GHz, supported by 12.0 GB of system memory and 260 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 processor implements AVX-512 vector extensions alongside AES cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark evaluations place single-core CPU throughput and cached memory transfers in the median tier, recorded at 1165.0 in Geekbench single-core and 421.33 GB/sec in small-block memory reads. However, shared core scheduling and low multi-core scaling constrain parallel throughput, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 3734.0 and a PassMark score of 6551.68. With a 1:3 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, bundled high-speed storage, and included IPv4 networking, this configuration aligns with lightweight application hosting, secondary database replicas, Redis caching instances, and CI/CD staging environments.
